title: router: apply route experiment selection before fallback policy evaluation
author: Elena Popov
description: Problem: When a route has both (a) a fallback policy (e.g., model fallback / region fallback) and (b) a route experiment (A/B variants), the router currently evaluates fallbacks first and only then attempts experiment selection. In practice that means experiments can be silently bypassed during mild capacity pressure or transient model health flips, and worse, attribution becomes misleading because traffic that should be split is instead routed via fallback and never hits the intended variant. This PR changes the routing order so experiment selection happens before fallback evaluation, while preserving safety behavior when experiment config is missing/invalid/unavailable. New order (high-level): 1) Resolve route + canonical route_id; 2) Evaluate eligibility + deterministic assignment for the experiment (if enabled and applicable) to pick a target variant; 3) Evaluate fallback policy for the selected variant target (model/region/tier) to ensure we still land on a healthy/available endpoint; 4) If fallback results in a different model/region than requested by variant, emit explicit metrics + debug fields so the results pipeline can reason about ‘variant overridden by fallback’. Safety/default behavior: If experiment evaluation fails closed (config fetch error, config not yet propagated, invalid variant configuration, missing stickiness key when required by policy), we fall back to the existing route default selection path and then evaluate fallback as before (i.e., no new failure mode for request routing). This is also gated behind the existing route-experiments feature flag in the router config so we can roll out gradually. Metrics added: router.route_experiments.pre_fallback_selected_total (count of requests where experiment assignment occurred prior to fallback), router.route_experiments.fallback_overrode_variant_total (count of requests where assignment happened but fallback changed the chosen target), router.route_experiments.assignment_error_total (assignment attempted but failed, labeled by error_type), and router.route_experiments.evaluator_latency_ms (timing for experiment evaluation). These metrics are emitted with low-cardinality tags (route_id, experiment_id, variant_id where present; region and model_id only on sampled spans per existing OTel conventions). Logging/attribution: The request context now retains both ‘assigned_variant’ and ‘final_routed_target’ so downstream telemetry can distinguish ‘variant traffic’ vs ‘variant selected but overridden’. This PR does not change the attribution schema itself (ADR-048); it ensures the router produces consistent assignment decisions earlier in the decision graph. Testing: Added unit tests covering precedence behavior and ensured existing fallback tests still pass. Added an integration test harness case that simulates a degraded primary model for one variant and validates that fallback occurs after assignment (and increments fallback_overrode_variant_total). Rollback plan: (1) flip router feature flag off to restore previous evaluation order without redeploy; (2) if needed, revert commit (safe: no persisted schema changes); (3) monitor SLO guardrails: error rate, p99 routing latency, and fallback_overrode_variant_total spike as a sign of misconfigured variants. Notes: This matches the decision captured in the routing/rollouts precedence discussion (apply experiment first, then allow fallback to preserve availability). This unblocks Console from showing meaningful ‘variant health’ even when fallbacks are active, because we can now measure how often a variant is being overridden rather than silently skipping the experiment.
commits: router: move experiment evaluator earlier in routing graph
router: carry assigned_variant + final_target through request context
metrics: emit pre-fallback selection + fallback override counters
tests: add precedence coverage for experiment vs fallback
docs(dev): add notes on precedence semantics for oncall debugging
conversation: Mina Haddad (review): Can we confirm the precedence with canary rollouts is unchanged? We need a single deterministic order when both are configured.

Elena Popov (author): Canary precedence stays the same; this PR only moves experiment evaluation earlier relative to fallback evaluation. Canary vs experiment precedence remains handled in route_decision_graph.ts (canary first, then experiment), and then fallback applies to whichever target was selected. I added an explicit test for canary+experiment+fallback ordering to make this less implicit.

Jordan Lee (review): Please ensure the bucketing inputs don’t change due to fallback (e.g., hashing model_id after fallback would break determinism). Assignment should be based only on stable request/route inputs.

Elena Popov (author): Agree. Assignment now happens before any target mutation, and the evaluator only uses {route_id, experiment_id, stickiness_key, salt}. No model_id/region inputs. Added a regression test that the hash inputs are identical regardless of fallback outcome.
Jada Williams (review): What happens if the experiment config fetch times out? We should not add tail latency to routing.

Elena Popov (author): Evaluator uses the cached config snapshot; if the snapshot is stale/unavailable we short-circuit to ‘no experiment applied’ in <1ms and increment assignment_error_total{error_type=cache_miss_or_stale}. No synchronous network call on request path.

Sean Gallagher (SRE review): Metrics cardinality risk: experiment_id + variant_id across all routes could blow up. Are we sampling any tags? Also add a metric for fallback override so we can alert if a variant is being completely masked.

Elena Popov (author): Tags follow the current experiment tagging guidance: route_id + experiment_id + variant_id only on metrics that are already per-experiment; model_id/region only on sampled spans. Added fallback_overrode_variant_total as requested; it’s low-cardinality and essential for dashboards/guardrails.
Rafael Mendes (review): Rollback plan looks good, but please add a note to the oncall doc about how to interpret ‘assigned_variant != final_target’. Support will ask.
Elena Popov (author): Added a short section to services/router/docs/oncall/route_experiments_precedence.md with examples and the metric mapping.
Mina Haddad (final): Approved. This aligns with the precedence decision and makes the routing behavior observable. Please coordinate with Logan/Caleb on dashboard wiring once merged.
Sean Gallagher (final): Approved with SRE sign-off given feature-flag gating + no new request-path dependencies.

Enable for staging + one internal account; verify router.route_experiments.pre_fallback_selected_total increments and assignment_error_total remains low.

If regressions: disable flag to restore prior order; if issues persist, revert squash commit.
release_notes: Routing precedence updated for route-level experiments: experiment assignment now occurs before fallback policy evaluation, improving split integrity and observability when fallbacks are active.
